name: Halflight
tagline: A title sequence that resolves into a page, printed in two inks and lit by the real sun over Oslo.
summary: The site opens like a film: shutters, a spark on a NASA horizon, a halftone field pulling focus into a photograph, then the name. Every surface after that is a two-ink duotone whose inks follow the actual solar altitude over Oslo, and visitors can drag the sun across today's sky to re-light the whole page. It reads as one person with cinematic ambition and the patience to get every frame right, which is what Albretsen AS sells.
voice: Title-card brevity, credits-roll calm: facts set like a film's opening credits, never a sales line. Example: "Software that pays for itself. Apps, SaaS and agent infrastructure, written and shipped from 59° north."
motion: Reveals sharpen rather than fade: everything moves from coarse to fine, over-exposed to printed, on long filmic ease-outs, and the letterbox only ever opens.
sound: Off until asked; then a soft three-voice drone tuned to the phase of day whose filter opens as the sun climbs, with a single 1.3 kHz glint when you grab the sun.
mark: A solid half-sun on the horizon over a tapering halftone reflection; it rises, prints its reflection dot by dot, then breathes (Lottie), beside an outlined Instrument Serif wordmark with a Geist Mono AS.
